newsitem.title: USA: AFL-CIO sues Calif. over unemployment insurance.
newsitem.headline: AFL-CIO sues Calif. over unemployment insurance.

text.p: The AFL-CIO said it filed a lawsuit Wednesday against California's employment department on behalf of at least 120,000 people who are allegedly deprived of $233 million in unemployment insurance each year.

The American Federation of Labor and Congress of Industrial Organizations (AFL-CIO) said it sued the California Employment Development Department on behalf of the workers, who either never receive their unemployment insurance or face delays of four to seven months before getting benefits.
The AFL-CIO has asked the U.S. District Court in San Francisco to certify the suit as a class action.

The AFL-CIO said the workers earned enough to qualify for unemployment benefits but are denied aid for up to seven months due to a California law. Under that law, the state ignores the recent earnings of the workers, the AFL-CIO said.
Thousands of workers need these earnings counted in order to qualify for benefits, the AFL-CIO said.

The AFL-CIO cited a state study that found that 28,200 Californians are forced onto state welfare because of the delay or denial of benefits. These delays shift the cost of unemployment from businesses, which fund unemployment, to taxpayers at a rate of $40 million in 1996, it said.

"Especially when the governor is proposing to shred the limited safety net, working people need and deserve this minimum unemployment insurance," California AFL-CIO Executive Secretary-Treasurer Art Pulaski said.
The Employment Development Department was not immediately available to comment on the lawsuit.
